The twelve source rows are Default (recommended), Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6. The picker shows eight rows at a time and scrolls the rest. Default is a provider-default sentinel, not an executable model id; its row and effort branch remain in evidence. Cats exposes the eleven explicit rows in picker order, with Opus selected by default as the operator requested earlier. This does not claim a provider-default alias will always resolve to Opus.
Display names are the exact picker labels, which carry the model version. Cats adds the status suffix ` (default)` in lowercase across model and effort menus; it is not part of the model name.

Execution values were observed per row: the agent chose a row for the session only (`s`, which left settings.json unchanged) and read the local `/status` Model line without submitting a prompt. On 2.1.285, Opus 5.5 sets `opus` (claude-opus-5-5), Sonnet 5.5 `sonnet` (claude-sonnet-5-5), and Sonnet 5 `claude-sonnet-5`. On 2.1.288 (2026-10-03) rows 2-12 were all re-read: Opus 5.5 `opus` (claude-opus-5-5), Fable 5.1 `fable` (claude-fable-5-1), Sonnet 5.5 `sonnet` (claude-sonnet-5-5), Haiku 4.5 `haiku` (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001), and each remaining row its full model id.

The `sonnet` alias moved from claude-sonnet-5 (2.1.282) to claude-sonnet-5-5; the Claude Code 2.1.284 changelog made Sonnet 5.5 the default Sonnet model. Entry `sonnet` keeps its id and its `sonnet` execution, so a saved selection keeps executing what it already did, and its label now follows the row that sets `sonnet`: Sonnet 5.5. Sonnet 5 is a new entry that executes `claude-sonnet-5`.

The picker no longer offers an Opus (1M context) row. `--model opus[1m]` still resolved to claude-opus-5-5[1m] on 2026-09-26, but the operator chose to follow the picker: Opus now executes `opus`, and its 1M label and limit are removed. The standard context value was not observed, so no limit is recorded. The operator also chose the picker's `claude-fable-5-1` over the `fable` alias; both resolved to claude-fable-5-1. Entry ids are unchanged. On 2.1.288 the Fable 5.1 row sets `fable` again (Claude Code 2.1.287: picking Fable now saves a value that follows the newest Fable). On 2026-10-03 the operator decided to keep `claude-fable-5-1`: the Fable 5.1 label then always matches the model that runs, while the alias would move to a newer Fable before the catalog is refreshed. Both still resolve to claude-fable-5-1.

Effort is one picker-wide selection. For each adjustable row, the capture pressed Right until the line returned to its starting level. Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5, Opus 4.8, and Opus 4.7 cycle Low, Medium, High, xHigh, and Max; Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 cycle Low, Medium, High, and Max only. Ultracode is no longer an effort level. Claude Code 2.1.284 made it a separate `/effort` toggle that no longer forces xhigh, and no 2.1.285 or 2.1.288 picker row offers it. The operator chose on 2026-09-30 to follow the picker and remove it. The 2.1.285 parser still accepts `--effort ultracode` as a legacy alias of `xhigh`, so a session bound earlier keeps a valid argument.

Effort descriptions on Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, and Sonnet 5.5 come from the Claude Code static artifact, not the picker. Low, Medium, High, and Max keep their earlier provenance and are unchanged in the 2.1.285 artifact; xHigh uses the 2.1.285 artifact text. The other rows carry only the observed Max warning.
Haiku 200K remains unverified 2.1.246 provenance. Context limits for the other rows were not observed and are omitted. Print mode (`-p`, which Cats uses) and other accounts were not probed.

The picker list appears to be remotely controlled. The openai-codex (ChatGPT subscription) channel of Pi 1.0.0: the models in the installed pi-ai registry (identical to the local model store refreshed 2026-10-03) that a ChatGPT account can run. Labels are the bare model ids, since the scope basis shows the openai-codex channel (operator decision 2026-09-29, replacing the <id> [openai-codex] labels); rows keep registry order; the selector only moves the current and a configured default model to the top. Other Pi providers are out of scope and remain available as custom provider/model strings.

The channel list is Pi's build-time catalog, not account entitlement. Pi also lists gpt-5.3-codex-spark, which is omitted: the same ChatGPT account's Codex CLI lists (0.156.1 on 2026-09-24, 0.160.0 on 2026-10-03) did not include it, and a Cats turn selecting it failed on 2026-09-29 with "The 'gpt-5.3-codex-spark' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account." It remains reachable as a custom provider/model string. gpt-6.1-sol, new in Pi 1.0.0, is in that Codex 0.160.0 list.

Thinking values per row are Pi's getSupportedThinkingLevels over each model's thinkingLevelMap, in Pi's order, labeled with Pi's tokens and thinking-selector descriptions. gpt-6-astra and gpt-6.1-sol have no off. Pi sends minimal as the low reasoning effort on every row here.

Pi's thinking selector marks the default thinking level (settings defaultThinkingLevel, or the built-in medium when unset), so medium is the control default. The model selector marks only a user-configured default model, so no row is a default and the UI initializes the first row.
Execution uses --provider openai-codex --model <raw ID> --thinking <level>. Limits are the registry contextWindow and maxTokens.

No model default is declared. The V3 config reports auto as the current model, meaning only the session's selection. --list-models reports default_model auto (plain output: * = default); that is recorded here as reference only and is not a catalog default.

Effort tokens are each row's effortLevels in the V3 config reply, which match the settings-panel ring of the 2.27.1 capture. Only the eleven rows with hasEffort carry kiro.reasoning_effort; rows without effort have controls: []. The low/medium/high/xhigh/max list in kiro-cli chat --help is global text, not per-model evidence.

Effort defaults are each row's defaultEffortLevel in the V3 config reply, adopted on 2026-10-13 under the operator's instruction to follow best practice: claude-opus-5.5 medium, claude-opus-4.7 xhigh, every other effort row high. Selection starts at that default and always sends --effort, which overrides chat.modelDefaults in ~/.kiro/settings/cli.json. The 2.27.1 picker had shown no default marker. The 2.30.0 V3 picker panel shows each row's current effort, not a marked default: it equals these defaults except where chat.modelDefaults saves another level.

The V3 config reply marks claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-4.8, claude-opus-4.7, claude-opus-4.6 and claude-sonnet-4.6 thinkingToggleable with thinking on by default, and the V3 picker panel shows thinking on for them. claude-opus-5.5 and claude-sonnet-5.5 are not toggleable: the 2.27.1 picker showed their thinking as Always on for this model, and the 2.30.0 V3 picker shows n/a, Not available for this model, the same text as rows without thinking. kiro-cli has no thinking argument, so the adapter cannot pass it and the axis is not represented.

Kiro 2.27.1 added a fallback row to every model's settings panel (none on every row: Answers for this model when it refuses or is unavailable). It selects another model rather than an option of this one, and it is not represented. The 2.30.0 V3 panel has no fallback row.

Context limits are --list-models context_window_tokens. Descriptions and credit rates are the config reply text, unchanged from the picker. Read on Windows native only: WSL shares this scope, but a WSL installation and account may see different models. Custom model strings remain available.

cli_version advanced from 2.30.0 to 2.31.0 on 2026-10-14 at the operator's request, without a new picker capture: kiro-cli chat --list-models and the V3 ACP probe listed exactly this scope's 21 entries in the same order, with the same effort levels and defaults. Thinking Level is the picker's thinking dialog, which offers every reasoning model the same five levels (Off, Low, Medium, High, Extra High) and preselects Medium. Execution passes --provider cline-pass --model <id> --thinking <level>; Cline then moves the level to the nearest effort the model advertises.

The complete Devin CLI 3000.11.3 model list, replacing the 2026-09-18 shortlist at the operator's request on 2026-10-14: every family of `devin models list --format json` in its order, except the fusion family (575 main-and-sidekick combinations) and the 17 legacy MODEL_* UIDs, which the operator excluded. 47 families with 246 variant UIDs remain. Speed Fast is the fast UID suffix on Claude rows and priority on GPT rows; both read Fast in the list. Value labels are the list's own wording, such as No Thinking and XHigh.
